content.value_statement: Teams need repeatable guidance for creating Claude Code skills without fragile activation rules. This skill explains triggers, hooks, guardrails, memory patterns, and troubleshooting steps.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to structure a SKILL.md file with frontmatter and clear activation language.
Documents keyword, intent, file path, and content trigger patterns for skill activation.
Describes hook behavior for UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, Stop, and related workflows.
Provides testing commands for validating trigger behavior and hook execution locally.
Covers memory-aware skill patterns, session tracking, skip conditions, and user controls.
Links to detailed references for troubleshooting, rule schemas, patterns, and advanced ideas.
limitations: It is documentation only and does not install or run hook code by itself.
Examples assume a Claude Code project layout with .claude directories and TypeScript hooks.
Commands must be adapted to each repository before use.
It does not replace manual review of hook behavior or security impact.

use_cases.title: Create a New Skill
use_cases.description: Use the guide to draft SKILL.md, add activation rules, test triggers, and keep guidance within recommended size limits.

use_cases.title: Tune Skill Activation
use_cases.description: Use the trigger references to reduce false positives and align keyword, intent, file, and content patterns.

use_cases.title: Document Team Guardrails
use_cases.description: Use the hook and enforcement guidance to document when skills should suggest, warn, or block risky workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a new Claude Code skill for our testing workflow. Include the SKILL.md outline and recommended trigger keywords.

prompt_templates.title: Add Activation Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add skill activation rules for a React frontend skill. Include keyword, intent, and file path trigger suggestions.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Trigger Behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: A skill is not activating for expected prompts. Walk through the checks for frontmatter, rules, hooks, and test commands.

prompt_templates.title: Design Memory-Aware Guardrails
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a memory-aware guardrail skill that tracks approved plans across sessions and gives users clear controls to view or clear memory.

output_examples.input: Create a backend development skill for our API project.
output_examples.output: A structured skill plan with frontmatter guidance, activation terms, rule suggestions, tests, and references for deeper backend standards.

output_examples.input: Our frontend skill activates too often on generic prompts.
output_examples.output: A focused troubleshooting path that narrows keywords, adds path exclusions, tests intent patterns, and checks hook registration.

output_examples.input: We want a skill to remember approved implementation plans.
output_examples.output: A memory-aware workflow design with storage locations, refresh triggers, user controls, and privacy boundaries.

best_practices: Keep the main SKILL.md concise and move detailed references into linked files.
Test triggers with real prompts and realistic file paths before publishing a skill.
Document skip conditions, memory storage, and user controls for any guardrail workflow.
anti_patterns: Using broad keywords that activate a skill for unrelated work.
Creating blocking guardrails without a clear recovery path for the user.
Storing sensitive data in skill memory or session files.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you design Claude Code skills with clear descriptions, activation rules, hooks, references, and testing steps.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides documented examples for local testing, but the skill itself is Markdown guidance.

faq.question: Which trigger types does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers keyword, intent, file path, and content triggers, plus guidance for avoiding false positives.

faq.question: Can it help with guardrail skills?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains block, suggest, and warn enforcement levels, with notes on skip conditions and user control.

faq.question: Does it support memory-aware skills?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents preference storage, plan workflows, session state, refresh triggers, and privacy limits.

faq.question: Is it specific to one project?
faq.answer: The examples use a Claude Code project layout, but the patterns can be adapted to similar repositories.
